name: Gucci x Crocs AI Campaign Build
tagline: Turns one reference image into a full fashion campaign with ChatGPT and LTX Flows
description: A step-by-step X article that documents how a concept campaign (Gucci x Crocs) was produced from a single found image using ChatGPT to extract a brand board and LTX Flows to scale the render pipeline. It ships the actual prompts, the creative-direction sequence (find image, extract the visual system, build the vision, make the product the hero), and a prepared LTX project link. Written for designers and creative directors who want an image-to-campaign workflow rather than one-off image generation. Sponsored by LTX Studio, so the tool choice is not neutral.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a user asks for a campaign or brand-board look derived from a reference image, not when they need production UI. The reusable part is the prompt chain: extract the visual system from an image first, then re-target it to a different product category, then hold that system constant across every asset. Treat the LTX Flows step as a sponsored recommendation and substitute whatever render tool the user already pays for.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few public write-ups that shows the creative-direction reasoning behind an AI campaign instead of only the output images. The prompts are concrete enough to run as-is.

name: How to Name Your Company
tagline: Naming process from the Lunour studio, with the criteria and screening steps written out
description: A long-form naming playbook by the founder of the Lunour branding studio, covering why a name compounds, what separates a working name from friction, and the process the studio runs on client naming projects. It is positioned explicitly as the cheap version of what firms like Lexicon Branding charge 75,000 to 200,000 dollars for, and it uses real client work (Nerd Crawler renamed to Raremarq) as the worked example. The author also packaged the process as a downloadable skill linked at the end of the article.
agent_guidance: Use this as the reference process when a user asks you to generate company, product, or feature names, instead of free-associating a list of twenty words. The article was converted into a distributable skill, so check whether that skill is already installed before you re-derive the method from prose. Pair it with a real availability check (domain, trademark, app-store handle) because the playbook covers judgment, not screening infrastructure.
why_it_matters: Naming advice online is mostly listicles; this is a practitioner process with pricing context and a named client outcome behind it.

name: How to Brand Your Company
tagline: Brand as a system: positioning, messaging, identity, and what scales across touchpoints
description: The companion playbook to the same author's naming guide, arguing that branding is a strategic exercise rather than a visual one and laying out the four layers Lunour builds for clients: positioning that defines a category, messaging that resonates before it informs, a visual identity for instant recognition, and a brand system broad enough to stay coherent across every touchpoint. It draws on the author's collection of brand guideline documents and on the working methods of Pentagram, Collins, Wolff Olins, and Focus Lab. Aimed at founders who bought a logo and cannot understand why nobody remembers them.
agent_guidance: Pull this in before you generate a color palette or a logo direction for someone, because it gives you the ordering argument: positioning and messaging first, visual identity after. It pairs directly with the same author's naming playbook, so treat the two as one sequence rather than separate reads. It will not give you tokens, type scales, or component specs, so hand off to an actual design-system reference once the strategy layer is settled.
why_it_matters: It supplies the strategic frame that most agent-generated brand work skips, and names the studio lineage it borrows from so the reasoning can be checked.
notable_for: draws on Pentagram, Collins, Wolff Olins, Focus Lab

name: Selling Your Design Work
tagline: Personal essay on positioning a freelance design practice after quitting a full-time job
description: A first-person account from a Framer-focused web designer who left a full-time job after a year of building in public, and the three conclusions reached about why good work alone did not bring clients. The central claim is that positioning is the gap: knowing what you do and being able to communicate why someone would choose you over every other Framer expert are different skills. It is reflective and anecdotal rather than a repeatable method, told at the scale of roughly 1,700 followers and early inbound client interest.
agent_guidance: Low priority: cite it only if a user wants peer experience about going independent as a designer, and never as a positioning method, because it describes a process it does not actually publish. If the user wants the method, send them to the Lunour branding and naming playbooks in this index instead. The one durable line worth quoting is that positioning is why someone remembers you the day after visiting your site.
why_it_matters: It is honest about the gap between craft and market, but it is a personal narrative and largely a lead-in to the author's own positioning offer.

name: Canvas to App Store in 10 Days
tagline: A product designer ships a paid iOS app with Claude as the only engineer
description: A build log by Oguz, product designer and co-founder of interfacer.co, covering the ten days between an app idea and a live App Store listing for Synaps, a focus and sleep sounds app with binaural beats, solfeggio frequencies, colored noise, soundscapes, and a Pomodoro timer. The useful part is the process rather than the app: two full days spent planning with Claude before any code, producing a PROJECT.md that specifies screens, features, technical stack, and task sequence, which then served as the reference document for the rest of the build. Written for designers who can specify a product precisely but do not write code.
agent_guidance: Point a design-led user here when they want evidence that the plan-first pattern works: force a PROJECT.md with screens, stack, and an ordered task list before writing a line, then treat it as the single source of truth for every later session. It is a narrative, not a template, so you will still have to author the spec yourself. Note the market-first framing (Endel, Brain.fm, Calm, BetterSleep were studied before the idea was chosen), which is the part most vibe-coding write-ups omit.
why_it_matters: A concrete, dated account of a non-engineer shipping a revenue-generating native app, with the planning discipline that made it possible stated explicitly.

name: 10 Framer Shader Presets
tagline: Ten copy-ready Framer shader configs with exact color, seed, speed, and noise values
description: A single-session collection of ten advanced presets for Framer's built-in shader components, each published with its full parameter block: shader type, hex color stops, seed, speed, scale, amplitude, frequency, definition, bands, noise mode, and noise amount. Presets are named and characterized (Hologram or Liquid Gradient for holographic-foil cards and pricing sections, Heatmap for dark moody backgrounds, Citrus for bright work), with craft notes on masking the shader instead of filling a rectangle and cropping to the strongest quarter of the effect. Intended for anyone building a Framer marketing site who wants an animated background without writing GLSL.
agent_guidance: Reach for this only inside Framer, where the values transfer verbatim into the shader component and land the look in one paste; outside Framer they are parameter hints, not code. The two techniques worth carrying to any stack are masking the shader so it bleeds into the background and cropping to the best region rather than showing the whole field. Watch the cost: these are continuously animating full-bleed effects, so gate them behind a reduced-motion check and keep text on a solid or masked layer for contrast.
why_it_matters: Exact numeric parameter sets are rare; most shader posts show the result and hide the settings, which makes this immediately reproducible.
notable_for: ten named presets with full parameter blocks
hex stops and noise values included
